title: REGENT: A Retrieval-Augmented Generalist Agent That Can Act In-Context in New Environments
context: retrieved state-action examples from expert demonstrations
action_mechanism: a transformer policy combines the query with retrieved neighbors
evidence: Evaluates adaptation to unseen environments using limited expert demonstrations; the paper assumes known state and action spaces.
why_it_matters: Makes retrieval an explicit baseline and context interface for cross-environment adaptation.
limitation: The paper assumes the state and action spaces of unseen environments are known.

title: Instant Policy: In-Context Imitation Learning via Graph Diffusion
context: one or two task demonstrations plus the current observation
action_mechanism: graph-based diffusion generates actions from demonstrations and observations
evidence: Reports simulated and real-robot tasks, with pseudo-demonstrations used for training.
why_it_matters: Tests whether structured geometric context can support immediate task imitation.
limitation: The pseudo-demonstration training recipe and few-shot test setup should not be conflated.

title: In-Context Imitation Learning via Next-Token Prediction
context: image, state, and action trajectories from teleoperated task demonstrations
action_mechanism: causal transformer autoregressively predicts sensorimotor tokens
evidence: Tests new prompt-specified tasks on a Franka robot, including changed environment configurations.
why_it_matters: Shows a sensorimotor sequence-model route to robot task adaptation without language or test-time parameter updates.
limitation: The reported robot setup is a Franka platform; cross-embodiment transfer is not established by this entry.

title: AMAGO: Scalable In-Context Reinforcement Learning for Adaptive Agents
context: prior observations, actions, and rewards over long rollouts
action_mechanism: long-sequence transformer policy conditions decisions on rollout history
setting: meta-RL and open-world agent benchmarks; adjacent to physical robotics
evidence: Reports meta-RL, long-term-memory, and goal-conditioned open-world evaluations, not physical-robot deployment.
why_it_matters: Provides an interaction-history comparison for demonstration-driven robot ICL.
limitation: The cited evaluations are agent benchmarks, not evidence of physical robot deployment.

title: VIMA: General Robot Manipulation with Multimodal Prompts
context: interleaved text and visual prompt tokens, including demonstration or goal information
action_mechanism: transformer autoregressively outputs motor actions conditioned on the prompt
evidence: Evaluates on procedurally generated tabletop tasks with a four-level generalization protocol.
why_it_matters: Unifies several task-specification formats within one multimodal prompt interface.
limitation: Multimodal prompting includes instructions and goals; prompt conditioning alone is not evidence of learning from examples.

title: One-Shot Imitation Learning
context: one demonstration of a new task
action_mechanism: meta-trained policy conditions action prediction on the demonstration
evidence: Introduces a meta-learning framework for one-shot imitation and evaluates robot manipulation tasks.
why_it_matters: An early reference point for adaptation from a single demonstrated task.
limitation: This early meta-learning setup does not establish broad cross-embodiment transfer.

title: ICI-VLA: In-Context Imitation with Spatiotemporally Aligned Demonstrations for Vision-Language-Action Models
context: retrieved short demonstrations aligned to the current subtask
action_mechanism: a fixed text-action VLM generates actions conditioned on retrieved examples
setting: LIBERO, RoboTwin 2.0, and four physical manipulation tasks
evidence: Reports simulation benchmark results and four physical task evaluations.
why_it_matters: Makes temporal and geometric alignment part of the retrieval interface.
limitation: Reported benchmark averages and physical task results use different protocols and must not be ranked together.

title: Zeva: In-Context Causal Learning for Generalizable Embodied Manipulation
context: stored action–effect signals from the robot’s own interactions
action_mechanism: retrieves causal interaction signals and injects them into a frozen policy
evidence: Reports simulation and real-world manipulation, including improvement as interaction experience accumulates.
why_it_matters: Separates learning from self-generated physical feedback from imitation of a teacher demonstration.
adaptation_target: physical condition and task from experience
limitation: The causal signal is model-derived; the paper’s term causal should not be read as an independently verified causal identification result.

title: In-Context World Modeling for Robotic Control
context: short task-agnostic, self-generated interaction history
action_mechanism: uses history to infer system variables before policy execution
evidence: Evaluates novel camera viewpoints in simulation and on real robot platforms.
why_it_matters: Shows that context can identify execution conditions rather than specify the task.
limitation: The abstract’s strongest explicit generalization result is on novel viewpoints; broader morphology transfer needs separate verification.

title: Behavior Prompting Policy: Demonstrations as Prompts for Manipulation
context: one human behavior demonstration and the current observation
action_mechanism: visuomotor policy translates a behavior prompt into robot actions
evidence: Evaluates DrawAnything and LIBERO-Gen and demonstrates a human using iPhUMI prompts to command a robot.
why_it_matters: Connects a user-facing demonstration interface with explicit unseen-task evaluations.
limitation: The paper’s new evaluation suites are not directly comparable with older benchmarks.

title: RoboSSM: Scalable In-context Imitation Learning via State-Space Models
context: a variable number of demonstrations, including longer prompts
action_mechanism: Longhorn state-space model conditions action prediction on demonstration history
evidence: Evaluates unseen and long-horizon LIBERO tasks and prompt-length extrapolation.
why_it_matters: Tests context length and architecture choice as central ICL design questions.
limitation: The cited evaluation is simulation; it does not establish physical robot performance.

title: RICL: Adding In-Context Adaptability to Pre-Trained Vision-Language-Action Models
context: relevant segments fetched from 10–20 demonstrations of a target task
action_mechanism: an ICL-trained VLA uses retrieved examples to generate actions
setting: new manipulation tasks with a pre-trained VLA
evidence: Reports improvements from 20 demonstrations per task without target-task parameter updates.
why_it_matters: Shows that an offline training recipe can add an in-context interface to an existing VLA.
limitation: The model is retrained offline for ICL; its no-update claim applies to the target task at deployment.

title: ReLIC: A Recipe for 64k Steps of In-Context Reinforcement Learning for Embodied AI
context: up to 64,000 steps of the agent’s observation and action history
action_mechanism: long-context attention uses experience to guide future navigation decisions
setting: embodied multi-object navigation in unseen simulated houses
evidence: Evaluates adaptation to unseen houses and few-shot imitation behavior in navigation.
why_it_matters: Makes context length and retained experience explicit in an embodied navigation setting.
limitation: The cited navigation results come from simulation rather than a physical robot.

title: Keypoint Action Tokens Enable In-Context Imitation Learning in Robotics
context: few-shot visual keypoint and action examples encoded as text tokens
action_mechanism: an off-the-shelf text model predicts tokenized action trajectories
evidence: Reports low-data comparisons on real-world everyday tasks without training the language model for robotics.
why_it_matters: Tests how far a token interface can carry visual-action examples into a language model.
limitation: The result depends on keypoint extraction and action-token design, not raw-image prompting alone.

title: Visual Memory for Robust Path Following
context: a demonstrated path compressed into a path abstraction
action_mechanism: a policy observes the world and uses the path abstraction to choose actions
setting: path following and homing in two simulators
evidence: Evaluates under actuation noise and environmental changes in two realistic simulators.
why_it_matters: An early navigation example where a route demonstration remains available as action-guiding memory.
limitation: This is route-conditioned navigation; evidence of broader task learning from examples is limited.

title: Bimanual Robot Manipulation via Multi-Agent In-Context Learning
context: few-shot bimanual examples represented for text-only language models
action_mechanism: leader–follower single-arm predictions coordinate two arms, with optional debate and judging
evidence: Evaluates few-shot bimanual manipulation on the TWIN benchmark.
why_it_matters: Shows one way to reduce the action-space burden of bimanual ICL for text-only models.
limitation: The cited benchmark result does not establish physical robot performance.

title: ICLR: In-Context Imitation Learning with Visual Reasoning
context: demonstrations augmented with visual reasoning traces of future image-space trajectories
action_mechanism: autoregressive transformer generates reasoning traces and low-level actions
evidence: Reports simulation and real-world tasks with unseen-task and novel-object evaluations.
why_it_matters: Tests whether explicit visual trajectory reasoning improves use of demonstration context.
limitation: The reasoning trace is a model representation; the reported success rate alone does not show human-interpretable causal reasoning.

title: In-Context Learning Enables Robot Action Prediction in LLMs
context: text descriptions of keyframes, object poses, and end-effector actions from examples
action_mechanism: an off-the-shelf text-only language model predicts robot actions from structured examples
evidence: Reports comparisons against zero-shot and ICL baselines in simulated and real-world settings.
why_it_matters: Exposes how much of robot action prediction can be carried by a structured text interface.
limitation: The result depends on heuristic keyframe selection, pose estimation, and textual conversion.

title: Prompting Decision Transformer for Few-Shot Policy Generalization
context: short trajectory segments from a few demonstrations
action_mechanism: a decision transformer conditions policy generation on trajectory prompts
evidence: Evaluates few-shot transfer on MuJoCo control tasks without target-task fine-tuning.
why_it_matters: A control-domain reference for demonstration prompts and prompt-length sensitivity.
limitation: The experiments are MuJoCo control benchmarks, not physical robot deployment.
context_budget: a few timesteps from demonstration trajectories

title: DemoDiffusion: One-Shot Human Imitation using pre-trained Diffusion Policy
context: one human demonstration supplying hand-motion trajectory
action_mechanism: kinematically retargets motion, then a pre-trained diffusion policy refines the robot trajectory
evidence: Reports real-world one-shot task results against the pre-trained policy and kinematic-retargeting baselines.
why_it_matters: Combines geometric motion transfer with a learned action prior without task-specific training.
limitation: The transferred trajectory depends on hand-motion extraction and kinematic retargeting quality.

title: One-Shot Imitation Learning with Invariance Matching for Robotic Manipulation
context: one unannotated demonstration of a novel manipulation task
action_mechanism: matches learned invariant regions between demonstration and test scene to infer end-effector poses
setting: RLBench novel tasks and one-shot sim-to-real robot demonstration
evidence: Reports 22 novel RLBench tasks and a one-shot sim-to-real result using a single real-robot demonstration.
why_it_matters: Makes geometric correspondence the main interface between demonstration and action.
limitation: The main aggregate evaluation is in RLBench; one-shot sim-to-real evidence has a narrower scope.

title: Zero-WAM: In-Context World-Action Modeling from Human Videos for Open-Ended Task Generalization
context: a human video that specifies the unseen manipulation task
action_mechanism: a causal video-action model generates robot actions conditioned on video guidance
setting: seven unseen RoboTwin 2.0 tasks and real-world manipulation
evidence: Reports unseen-task RoboTwin 2.0 simulation and physical evaluations with human video guidance.
why_it_matters: Examines human video as a task-specification interface for a world-action model.
limitation: Future-chunk prediction is a training objective; the deployment claim concerns video-guided action, not necessarily pixel decoding.

title: Decompose and Recompose: Reasoning New Skills from Existing Abilities for Cross-Task Robotic Manipulation
context: retrieved demonstrations represented as atomic skill–action pairs
action_mechanism: recomposes skill sequences and execution order for a new task
evidence: Reports zero-shot cross-task evaluations in AGNOSTOS and physical settings.
why_it_matters: Moves contextual evidence from low-level trajectories to composable skill structure.
limitation: The reported zero-shot transfer relies on a demonstration library and planning-agent-generated skill sequences.
